transport: RS-485 on the 8-pin CT/RS485/DRM0/ESTOP connector. Documented pinout: pin1 CT+, pin2 CT-, pin3 METER485-, pin4 METER485+, pin5 GND, pin6 DRM0, pin7 NC, pin8 ESTOP. Baud, framing, and slave ID are NOT stated. Named meter is Eastron SDM230-Modbus; named CTs are EM-EICT-120K-T210C and CTSA016.
sharedMapEvidence: The Force Series (F-G2) User Manual, revision 20260225, section 1.1 Scope: 'the following model(s) of Energizer products: Force 3S, Force 3.6S, Force 4.6S, Force 5S, Force 6S'. One communication chapter and one pinout table cover all five. Shared wiring only — no register map published for any of them.
gotchas: CONTRADICTION, recorded not resolved: the manual's prose says 'RS485 is a standard communication interface which can transmit the real time data from inverter to PC or other monitoring devices' — implying an inverter data bus — but the only pins the pinout table labels are METER485- / METER485+. The manual does not say
Grid-tie only, 230 V single phase. No battery port, so nothing to report about a bank.
Firmware paths in the manual are Update\master, Update\slave, Update\manager .hex — a three-MCU architecture. Same structure appears across the Force lines.
The manual is a 2026 revision but the copyright block still reads '© 2022 Energizer ... used under license by 8 Star Energy Pty Ltd'.
